checkout-api.title: Checkout 5xx surge / elevated error rate
steps: Confirm the blast radius on the Checkout API dashboard (error rate by region and by pod).
Check whether the errors correlate with a deploy in the last 4 hours; if so, roll back first and investigate after.
Inspect ledger-service dependency health -- checkout returns 503 when ledger write latency exceeds 2s.
If ledger is healthy, check the payments Postgres connection pool saturation metric.
Shed load by enabling the checkout queue-and-retry feature flag if the error rate stays above 10%.

checkout-api.title: Checkout latency degradation
steps: Compare p50/p95/p99 against the 7 day baseline on the Checkout API dashboard.
Break the latency down by downstream call -- ledger-service, fraud-scoring, Postgres.
If fraud-scoring is the contributor, enable fail-open mode; fraud scoring is permitted to fail open.
If Postgres is the contributor, check for long-running queries and recent schema migrations.
Scale the checkout deployment out if CPU throttling is observed on more than 20% of pods.

ledger-service.title: Ledger write failures or posting backlog
steps: STOP: never restart the ledger writer without first capturing the pending posting queue depth.
Verify the partitioned posting table migration completed on every replica.
Check for replication lag on postgres-payments; ledger writes block when lag exceeds 30s.
If lag is the cause, fail over to the healthy replica and page Data Platform.
Reconcile the posting journal before declaring the incident resolved.
ledger-service.escalate_to: Payments Core incident commander AND Data Platform primary

fraud-scoring.title: Fraud scoring latency or model regression
steps: Check the model rollout percentage; v7 is currently a partial rollout.
Compare score distribution between v6 and v7 cohorts on the fraud dashboard.
If v7 shows a regression, set the rollout percentage back to 0.
Enable fail-open mode so checkout is not blocked while investigating.
Notify Risk Platform and open a model regression ticket.

notification-gateway.title: Notifications delayed or not delivered
steps: Check the provider status page before investigating internally.
Inspect the outbound queue depth; delivery is best-effort within 5 minutes.
Replay failed messages from the dead letter queue once the provider recovers.
This is a tier-3 service -- do not page outside business hours unless it is blocking a tier-1 incident.

postgres-payments.title: Payments Postgres availability or replication incident
steps: Identify the primary and confirm whether an automatic failover has already occurred.
Check replication lag and WAL disk usage on every replica.
Terminate long-running queries above 60s only after capturing the query plan.
If disk pressure is the cause, expand the volume before failing over.
RPO is 5 minutes and RTO is 30 minutes -- declare a SEV1 if either is at risk.
postgres-payments.escalate_to: Data Platform primary on-call AND the incident commander
